picks.title: Suno Says Jason Isbell Lawsuit Over Artist 'Identities' Must Be Dismissed: 'Nothing Unlawful About That'
picks.rationale: New court filing: Suno's motion to dismiss argues prompting for an artist's style is lawful, a defense that decides whether style prompts stay legal for creators.
picks.excerpt: Suno filed a motion to dismiss Jason Isbell's class action alleging the AI music platform stole the artistic identities of Isbell and other artists, arguing there is 'nothing unlawful' about letting users prompt for an artist's style.

picks.title: Music industry intervenes in Open AI's big legal battle with newspapers and authors
picks.rationale: New amicus filing by RIAA, NMPA, A2IM and others against fair-use AI training, the same question that decides the Suno, Udio and Anthropic music suits.
picks.excerpt: RIAA, NMPA, A2IM, SONA and ARA filed an amicus brief in the authors' and newspapers' case against OpenAI, setting out why AI training should never be fair use - the same question that decides the labels' suits against Suno, Udio and Anthropic.

picks.title: Disney has fought AI firms over copyright. Now it's testing AI lyric videos.
picks.rationale: A major rightsholder starts using generative video on its own music catalog (OpenArt lyric videos, Hercules), a concrete new deployment rather than commentary.
picks.excerpt: Disney is working with AI startup OpenArt to conceptualize lyric videos, starting with 'Go the Distance' from Hercules - a test of generative video on its own music catalog.

picks.title: Slop Till You Drop: A Peek at the iTunes U.S. Top 10
picks.rationale: Four seemingly AI-aided tracks in the Nov. 1 US iTunes Top 10, including the Suno-made No. 1; HITS maps where AI ends and human production begins.
picks.excerpt: The Nov. 1 iTunes U.S. Top 10 had four tracks seemingly made with AI aid, including the No. 1 'Tell Me, How Is Heaven' by May the Lord Studio; HITS listened through to map where AI ends and human music-making begins.

picks.title: Seoul Music Forum explores humanism in AI age, with one in four K-pop acts now virtual
picks.rationale: Hard industry stat from the 2026 Seoul Music Forum: 10 of 45 new K-pop debuts this year are virtual acts, showing AI idols entering the mainstream pipeline.
picks.excerpt: The 2026 Seoul Music Forum examined AI's rise in music, citing that one in four new K-pop acts this year is virtual and debating what it means for labels and creators.

https://www.billboard.com/pro/suno-respo.new_action: Suno filed a motion to dismiss Jason Isbell's artist-identity class action (new court filing; the Isbell suit itself was never published).
